subject: biology

resources.title: Biology 2e
resources.notes: Broad introductory biology textbook. Foundation mapping is limited to introductory/review use; it does not imply every chapter is foundation-level.

resources.title: Fundamentals of Biology
resources.notes: MIT OCW Scholar course designed for independent study with no formal prerequisites; includes lecture excerpts, problems with solutions, concept quizzes, help-session videos, and study terms.

resources.title: Introductory Biology
resources.notes: Undergraduate course with lecture videos, problem sets and solutions, exams, and study materials; includes molecular genetics, cell biology, imaging, immunology, bacteria and viruses.

resources.title: Introductory Biology
resources.notes: Undergraduate biology course emphasizing genomic approaches to human biology, development, immunology, tissue repair, stem cells, tissue engineering, infectious and inherited disease.

resources.title: 7.28x Molecular Biology
resources.notes: In-depth molecular biology course on genome maintenance, expression and evolution, including DNA replication and repair, transcription, transposition, RNA processing and translation; problem sets and quizzes develop experimental-design and data-analysis skills.

resources.title: Cell Biology: Transport and Signaling
resources.notes: Experimental-level cell biology focused on cellular transport and signaling mechanisms, regulation, hypothesis testing, and interpretation of experiments.

resources.title: NCBI Bookshelf
resources.notes: Reference library and discovery source; individual books require rights and edition verification and do not by themselves establish mastery.

resources.title: PubMed
resources.notes: Primary literature discovery index; indexing access is not equivalent to verified research competence.

resources.title: PubMed Central
resources.notes: Full-text research archive with article-specific licenses; research availability does not substitute for assessment, laboratory practice, or expert-readiness verification.

known_gaps: Dedicated foundation-level curricula remain thin outside broad introductory biology.
Evolution and ecology need stronger dedicated course-level evidence across advanced, graduate, and research levels rather than relying primarily on a broad textbook.

Systems biology, neuroscience, bioinformatics, microbiology, and developmental biology need additional dedicated advanced or graduate instructional resources where exact taxonomy cells remain uncovered.

Expert readiness still requires laboratory or computational practice, primary-literature evaluation, reproducible analysis, working retrieval and citation provenance, and passed assessment; research indexes alone do not satisfy that gate.
